note: The strict rerun rule's script, scripts/mutants-due.py. Each mutant switches off one path by which a change makes a mutant file due; the judges are the self-test and the three real runs against this tree -- a header between a mutant and its tests (core/Scalar.hpp, which must make m1-12 and m1-87 due, the second only through its headers), a shader no mutant touches (which must make m1-13 due through its application judge), and a script on a ctest command line (which must make m1-15 due). Since M1-109 (register decision 392) a Python mutant names no build target, and the harness builds nothing for it; until then every mutant named orbsim_shaders as a no-op, which made every shader an input of this file. Not mutated: the line that adds each mutated file to its own inputs, because every mutated file here is also reached another way -- its judges are built from it, or read it at run time, or it is in the always-due set -- so removing that line changes no verdict in this repository; and mutate.py's record_pass, which only the harness itself exercises, checked by hand instead (a pass over an uncommitted tree must say 'pass not recorded'). **First run, 2026-09-27: 5 caught, 2 survived.** 'An expected file that is not due is not reported' was a real hole -- every real run expected a file that is due -- closed by mutants_due_unmet_expectation_fails, which must fail. 'Shaders are no longer an input' is equivalent here and declared, on the owner's ruling (decision 218). **Second run, 2026-09-28, with the must-fail test among the judges: 6 caught, 1 survived as declared, none invalid, none hung.** **2026-09-30, M1-103 (register decision 250)**: the mutant "the build definition is no longer always an input" is removed. Under M1-103 the build definition makes a file due only through a changed judge fingerprint, or where none was recorded, so that mutant is now the rule rather than a defect; its concern -- that a build-definition change is not ignored -- is carried by m1-103.json, whose mutants take away the fallbacks.

mutants.name: a file with no recorded pass is not due
mutants.find:
if not recorded:
        return True, ["no recorded pass"]

mutants.name: a changed input does not count
headers from Ninja's log are ignored
shaders are no longer an input of the application's judges
mutants.why: Declared surviving from 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-05, on the owner's ruling (register decision 218): `ninja -t inputs orbsim.exe` listed all 7 shader sources then, because orbsim depends on orbsim_shaders for its build order, so removing the run-time path changed no verdict, and the path was kept as a safeguard for the day that build-order dependency changed. M1-109 is that day (register decision 393): build-order edges are no longer followed, the run-time path is the only one by which a shader reaches a test that starts the application, and this mutant is expected caught -- by mutants_due_shaders, among others.

mutants.name: files on a ctest command line are ignored
an expected file that is not due is not reported
mutants.find: return 1 if missing or listed else 0
